extracted.intended_audience: poets, students, and general readers interested in poetry
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for identifying and composing blank verse: unrhymed iambic pentameter (10-syllable lines) commonly used in English dramatic and epic poetry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form name / alternative name
rubrics_metrics.description: Blank verse — also called heroic verse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that 'heroic verse' is an alternative name sometimes used for blank verse; identity of form is tied to meter and rhyme (or lack thereof).

rubrics_metrics.name: Unrhyming (no end rhyme)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unrhyming iambic pentameter — blank verse is by definition unrhymed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating or composing blank verse, do not add end rhymes; the absence of rhyme distinguishes it from other pentameter forms like heroic couplets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Iambic pentameter (ten-syllable line)
rubrics_metrics.description: This 10-syllable line is the predominant rhythm of traditional English dramatic and epic poetry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lines should generally follow iambic pentameter (five iambic feet ≈ ten syllables). Meteric regularity toward iambic pentameter is the defining metrical requirement for blank verse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Natural, speech-like rhythm
rubrics_metrics.description: Blank verse is considered the closest to English speech patterns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the form when seeking a rhythm that approximates natural English speech—this makes it suitable for dramatic monologues and long narrative/epic passages where conversational cadence is desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typical contexts and canonical examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Predominant rhythm of traditional English dramatic and epic poetry; examples include John Milton’s Paradise Lost, Robert Browning’s dramatic monologues, and Wallace Stevens’s “Sunday Morning.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referencing these canonical works can guide tone, scale, and use: blank verse is well suited to extended narrative and dramatic forms; browse additional blank verse poems for exemplars.
